WF-03 Step 3 idiom/scope gate for ISS-0119's fix (implementation commit 8ad3bb4: 11 files, 349 insertions, 32 deletions). SECURITY-REVIEWER passed at Step 3c with all eight invariants dispositioned and the change ruled out of scope on evidence (zero .ex/.exs files, zero migrations in the branch diff).

YOUR ORDINARY GATE FIRST. Review `git diff main...HEAD` for scope creep, internal consistency, and consistency with `docs/migration/decisions/` records. This change rewrites instruction text across nine docs and agent role files -- that is a large blast radius for a WF-03 fix, so the scope-creep question is real and not pro forma: did the implementation edit anything the design did not specify, and did it edit any site in a way that changes a rule rather than repointing it at the new volume layout? Verify against §10's post-edit text rather than against the commit message.

THEN THREE THINGS ONLY YOU CAN DECIDE.

(1) DECISION ITEM F1 -- A GENUINE DEFECT IN THE APPROVED DESIGN, and the reason this handoff is HIGH priority. ELIXIR-DEV found it, verified it byte-wise, and correctly REPORTED it rather than silently diverging (its handoff was explicitly told a disagreement is worth surfacing, not absorbing). §8 of the design gives three implementations of the frozen_prefix_sha256 and states all three must agree. THEY DO NOT. The Bash normative form and the PowerShell form both yield 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804 -- which CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently computed at re-gate pass 2, and which ELIXIR-DEV reproduced before and after the append, so volume 1 is confirmed intact. The §8 ELIXIR form returns 5c9fda42...657a instead. Diagnosed cause: `File.stream!/1` opens in text mode on Windows and has already stripped the CR, so `String.trim_trailing(&1, "\r\n")` -- which trims only that exact two-byte suffix -- matches nothing, the surviving `\n` remains, and the `<> "\n"` appends a second one, for exactly +5,766 bytes. ELIXIR-DEV states the corrected form `String.trim_trailing(&1, "\n") |> String.trim_trailing("\r")` reproduces the normative value, verified. WHY THIS MATTERS AND WHY IT IS URGENT: assertion A6 is the first mechanical enforcement the append-only rule has ever had, and TEST-DESIGNER implements it at Step 4 from §8. Left as written, A6 goes red on every Windows checkout while pointing at the wrong artefact -- a false alarm on the exact safeguard this whole run exists to restore, which is worse than no assertion at all because it trains readers to ignore it. YOUR RULING: is the correction (a) a design defect requiring CODE-DESIGNER rework, or (b) a verified erratum that TEST-DESIGNER applies at Step 4 while correcting §8 in the same pass, recorded as such? ORCH's constraint, stated so you can weigh it and NOT so it decides the matter for you: step-02's rework_count is already 2 of max_rework 3, so a third iteration would trip ORCHESTRATOR.md §5's escalation threshold and stop the run. ORCH will not route around a gate to avoid that -- if you rule (a), the run escalates and that is the correct outcome. Rule on the merits.

(2) OPEN QUESTION #3 from the design's §12, routed to you at Step 2b and still unanswered: the invariant test runs under plain `mix test` (and therefore `mix letflow.check`'s test step) with no database. Should it ALSO be a standalone `mix letflow.check` step, so a docs-only change is gated without running the full suite? The design calls this a REVIEWER call, not a design decision. Note the live context that makes it concrete: `mix letflow.check` is currently RED for unrelated reasons (see item 3), so a docs-only invariant that can only be observed through a red full suite is observable in principle and not in practice.

(3) THE RED GATE, and whether it blocks this run. ELIXIR-DEV ran `mix letflow.check`: toolchain check, `format --check-formatted` and `compile --warnings-as-errors` all exit 0; the test step reports 1259/1274 passed, 15 failed. Its attribution, which you should test rather than accept: this commit changes zero .ex/.exs files; the only reference to any file it touches anywhere in lib/ or test/ is a @moduledoc string in a test that passed; the root cause was pinned by direct query to orphaned rows in `public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup` in the persistent Docker volume whose parent `tenants` rows are gone, and deleting them cut one file from 12 failures to 3; Postgres was also at max_connections saturation after 11h uptime. Decisively, `test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml` already records the identical constraint, table and frame for `main`, and `docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml` is status `instrumented` -- diagnosed, not fixed, with successor ISS-0116 carrying the remaining work. core-directives.md's 'Never Call a Red Pipeline OK Without a Source' forbids attributing a red result on judgement alone; here a source is claimed, so your job is to confirm the source actually says what it is claimed to say, and to state whether this branch ADDS any failure that main does not already have. That last point is the one that decides whether Step Final may proceed. If you cannot establish it from the existing report, say so -- TEST-RUNNER can establish the baseline at Step 4c.

Also disposition ELIXIR-DEV's two INFO items: §10.6's AGENT_SYSTEM.md:105 replacement leaves volume 1 as the sentence subject (ELIXIR-DEV used the design's exact text rather than improving it, which was the correct instruction-following call -- your question is whether the resulting sentence is now misleading), and one TASK_QUEUE.md line was re-wrapped with a newline moved and no word changed.

Do not edit any file other than your own handoff. If you rule (b) on F1, do NOT apply the correction yourself -- state it precisely enough for TEST-DESIGNER to apply.

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 3d REVIEWER gate for ISS-0119: PASS, with 3 MINORs and 2 conditions on Step 4. No BLOCKER. Everything below was run on this host; nothing is inherited from ELIXIR-DEV's handoff.

=== A. ORDINARY GATE -- SCOPE CREEP, CONSISTENCY, DECISION RECORDS ===

OTP-idiom and supervision questions are N/A by construction: `git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- '*.ex' '*.exs' lib/ priv/ config/ mix.exs mix.lock test/` returns exactly ONE path and it is markdown (lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md). Zero gen_statem, zero supervisor, zero schema, zero migration. Same evidence SECURITY-REVIEWER used at 3c, re-derived rather than copied.

SCOPE CREEP: NONE FOUND. Verified against section 10's post-edit text, not the commit message.
 - File set matches section 11 exactly: 9 modified + 2 created (v2, index). The 2 test files section 11 lists were correctly NOT created -- ORCH routed them to Step 4, and ELIXIR-DEV said so instead of building them. No file outside section 11 was touched except run bookkeeping (handoffs/*, registry.json, the design artefact itself).
 - All 16 EDIT sites in section 10.1 are present and none is missing: CLAUDE.md:85; core-directives :173, :290, :328; doc-updater :17, :31, :47; release-validator :23; AGENT_SYSTEM :46, :105, :136; WF-02 :106, :390; TASK_QUEUE :133, :379; anti-patterns (rewrite + new entry). All 8 NO-CHANGE sites are untouched.
 - VERBATIM CHECK, mechanical not eyeballed: diff of the design's section 4 fenced block (lines 263-393, CR-stripped) against docs/status/requirement_status.v2.yaml -> the ONLY difference is the design's opening ```yaml fence line. Volume 2 is byte-identical to section 4. The index is byte-identical to section 3.3 with the placeholder "<computed at Step 3 -- see design section 8>" replaced by the real digest and nothing else. Volume 1's footer is byte-identical to section 3.1.
 - NO SITE CHANGES A RULE RATHER THAN REPOINTING IT, beyond what the design sanctions. Two sites do change rules and both are the design's own approved content, not implementer invention: core-directives:328's precedence paragraph (section 9 + section 10.3 -- the :173-vs-:328 ruling this run exists to make) and TASK_QUEUE:133's field correction (section 10.4 -- SCOPE-CHANGE is a `req:` value, never an `event:` value). Every other edit repoints a path and nothing else.
 - Volume 1 append-only: `git diff --numstat main...HEAD -- docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` -> "38  0". Insertions only, independently re-run here.
 - I re-verified section 8 check 3 myself, the one that protects an immutable citation: the frozen prefix's digest reproduces (below), which subsumes line 5158 and the three anomalies bit-for-bit.

DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY: CHECKED, CONSISTENT, no divergence and no disagreement to register. All seven records read against the diff. None of 0001 (web framework), 0002 (OIDC), 0003 (Ecto schema strategy), 0005 (pin/formatting toolchain), 0006 (identity tables), 0007 (variable merge) has any surface here -- the change touches no runtime code, no dependency, no schema. 0004-humanless-pipeline.md is the one record that IS engaged, and this change moves toward it, not away: 0004's central claim is that with no human backstop every rule needs a mechanical second line of defence, and this run converts the append-only rule from an eyes-only convention into an asserted invariant. The new anti-patterns entry states that reasoning in 0004's own terms. Nothing here re-decides anything a record settled.

=== B. F1 -- RULING: (b) VERIFIED ERRATUM, applied by TEST-DESIGNER at Step 4 ===

FIRST, INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED ON THIS HOST. I did not take ELIXIR-DEV's numbers on trust; I ran all three forms myself:
  Bash (normative):    head -n 5766 SF | tr -d '\r' | sha256sum
                       -> 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804
  section 8 Elixir AS WRITTEN -> 5c9fda42d72b0d46e4bf60cfc5a0fc044d7c36eb0192bc4b5e599c2a559b657a   (361,376 bytes)
  section 8 Elixir CORRECTED  -> 5a1a64ab0b999da3fd86be90109ecee46b9d538d9e9945c0d39fddb10075a804   (355,610 bytes)
  delta = 361,376 - 355,610 = 5,766 = exactly one byte per line, confirming the diagnosis mechanically and not by narrative.
  Also confirmed the mechanism directly: File.stream! yields line 1 as "# RoCo -- Requirement run history\n" -- terminator is a bare \n on a CRLF checkout, so String.trim_trailing(&1, "\r\n") (which trims that exact two-byte suffix) matches nothing and <> "\n" doubles it. ELIXIR-DEV's diagnosis is correct in every particular. The value committed in the index is the correct one.

RULING: (b). Reasoning on the merits:
 1. WHAT IS WRONG IS AN ILLUSTRATION, NOT THE SPECIFICATION. Section 8 defines the hashed byte stream normatively in prose ("terminate EVERY line with a single \n, including the last"), designates the Bash form as normative, and then -- decisively -- pre-adjudicates this exact case in its own text: "(If they do not, the defect is in the implementation, not in this convention.)" The convention is right, unambiguous, and is what both the gate and the shipped index value were computed from. One of three non-normative reference expressions of it is wrong. That is the textbook shape of an erratum.
 2. THERE IS NO DESIGN DECISION LEFT OPEN. Rework exists to re-decide something, or to make an unbuildable artefact buildable. Neither applies: nothing about layout, precedence, the assertion set, the roll rule or scope changes, and the artefact was in fact built from it. A rework cycle would return the identical 1,004-line document with two tokens different -- a correction that is already verified, twice, on two agents' runs.
 3. BLAST RADIUS IS ONE FILE THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET. The only consumer of the Elixir form is StatusHistory.frozen_prefix_digest/2, which TEST-DESIGNER writes at Step 4. No committed artefact depends on it. Nothing needs unwinding.
 4. THE URGENCY ARGUES FOR (b), NOT AGAINST IT. A6 is the first mechanical enforcement the append-only rule has ever had. The failure mode of shipping section 8 as written is a permanently-red assertion pointing at the wrong artefact on every Windows checkout -- which trains readers to ignore the one safeguard this run exists to restore. (b) removes that risk in the very next step; (a) leaves the repo with no invariant test at all while the design is re-issued.
 5. COUNTER-ARGUMENT, WEIGHED AND REJECTED. Section 8 was approved by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at Step 2, so a defect in it is a gate escape, and "gate escapes go back to the producer" is a clean rule. But the gate's job was to certify the design is unambiguous and buildable, and on the evidence it IS -- the ambiguity that mattered (which digest convention) was resolved correctly and the gate itself independently computed the right value. Treating a verified two-token editorial error as equivalent to a wrong decision would apply the rework mechanism to something it was not built for.
 6. ESCALATION CONSTRAINT: acknowledged, and NOT decisive. I would rule (b) with step-02's rework_count at 0. ORCH stated it so I could weigh it, and it carried no weight -- (1) through (5) are sufficient on their own, and if they had pointed at (a) I would have ruled (a) and let the run escalate.

THE CORRECTION, STATED PRECISELY SO TEST-DESIGNER INVENTS NOTHING. Replace section 8's Elixir bullet with:
  - Elixir (the test): File.stream!(path) |> Enum.take(n) |> Enum.map_join("", &((&1 |> String.trim_trailing("\n") |> String.trim_trailing("\r")) <> "\n")) |> then(&:crypto.hash(:sha256, &1)) |> Base.encode16(case: :lower)
ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: trim "\n" FIRST, then "\r". Never the literal two-byte "\r\n". Rationale to carry into the note: File.stream!/1 opens in text mode, so on a CRLF checkout the CR is already gone and only "\n" is present; on an LF checkout or a binary-mode read the line ends "\r\n" and the two-step trim removes both. The two-step form is therefore correct in BOTH cases, which is what makes it portable between this Windows host and CI. Verified above: it reproduces the normative digest exactly, 355,610 bytes.

CONDITIONS ON THIS RULING (both required; without them the ruling is not (b), it is "ignore it"):
  C1. TEST-DESIGNER uses the corrected form in StatusHistory.frozen_prefix_digest/2, and quotes the digest its test actually computes alongside the normative Bash value in its handoff. A6 must be observed green, not predicted green -- CHECK 5 of section 8 could not be completed at Step 3 (ELIXIR-DEV correctly said so rather than claiming a green it never saw), so Step 4 is where that check is finally discharged.
  C2. TEST-DESIGNER corrects section 8's Elixir bullet in the SAME commit, inline, with a one-line note recording it as an erratum ruled by REVIEWER at Step 3d of run WF03-ISS0119-20260821. The design artefact and the shipped test must not disagree; an erratum that lives only in a handoff is exactly the "recorded where no one lands" failure this run is about.
  MINOR alongside C1 (no action, recorded so it is not rediscovered): the Elixir and Bash forms would diverge if the hashed prefix's LAST line carried no terminator (head emits none in that case; the Elixir form appends one). Not reachable here -- the prefix ends at line 5,766 of a 5,804-line file -- so no guard is required. If a future volume is ever hashed to its own EOF, this becomes live.

=== C. OPEN QUESTION #3 -- ANSWER: NO. Do not add a standalone `mix letflow.check` step. ===
Reasons, in order of weight:
 1. SCOPE CREEP, on my own mandate item 4. `mix letflow.check` is shared project-wide plumbing; every step added to it is paid by every run forever. One docs invariant, on the day it is first written, has not earned a top-level gate step. This is generic machinery ahead of demonstrated need -- exactly what I am here to flag, and I would flag it identically if someone else proposed it.
 2. IT WOULD RUN THE ASSERTION TWICE. The test already executes under plain `mix test`, which IS letflow.check's test step. A separate step re-runs the same assertions in a different invocation, and two runs that can disagree (different cwd, env, working-tree state) is a worse diagnostic surface than one, not a better one.
 3. THE STATED NEED IS REAL BUT ALREADY MET. "Gate a docs-only change without the full suite" is answered today by `mix test test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs` -- targeted, no database, seconds. A new gate step adds nothing that command does not already provide.
 4. THE LIVE RED-GATE CONTEXT CUTS THE OTHER WAY FROM HOW THE QUESTION FRAMES IT. That letflow.check is red for unrelated reasons is an argument for keeping the invariant INDEPENDENTLY runnable -- which it is -- not for welding it onto the same red gate, where it would inherit ISS-0109's noise and become unobservable in exactly the way the question worries about.
NON-BINDING SUGGESTION (not a condition, do not treat it as required work): doc-updater.md's Forbidden paragraph already names test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs; whoever next edits that file could cheaply name the one-line command to run it. Out of scope for this run.
REVISIT TRIGGER, recorded so this stays a decision and not a preference: if a docs-only change ever merges past a broken invariant because nobody ran the suite, that is evidence, and the answer changes.

=== D. THE RED GATE -- SOURCE CONFIRMED WITH ONE CORRECTION; VERDICT: THIS BRANCH ADDS NO FAILURE MAIN DOES NOT ALREADY HAVE ===

SOURCE CHECK, read rather than assumed. test/reports/report-20260821-WF03-ISS0109-20260821.yaml DOES say what it is claimed to say, for the part that carries the weight:
 - 10 x Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest: Postgrex 23503 foreign_key_violation on constraint tenant_schemas_tenant_id_fkey, orphan sourced from public.iss060_tenant_schemas_guard_backup, failing frame restore_orphaned_guard_backup_rows!/0 at identity_migration_test.exs:242. Report marks it ATTRIBUTED on a four-axis match (module + all ten test names + error class + frame) against two earlier baselines, and records "caused_by_this_branch: NO -- pre-existing". Same constraint, same table, same frame ELIXIR-DEV quotes.
 - The orphaned UUID matches ELIXIR-DEV's exactly: ba8fb4e0-34db-46d1-a5ef-616571e2a468. The report explains why (that run used this same workspace DB, letflow-2-postgres-1 on port 5472). Consistent, and the report was candid that its own baselines carried a different UUID.
 - 3 x Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest 60s ExUnit.TimeoutError: present (2 baseline-matched, 1 explicitly "ATTRIBUTED BY CLASS ONLY").
 - docs/issues/ISS-0109.yaml: status `instrumented`, superseded_by ISS-0116; ISS-0116 is status `open`. Diagnosed, not fixed -- as claimed.
CORRECTION TO THE CLAIM, since precision is the point of this check: the report is for branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821 at commit 12286e8, NOT literally for main. It is accurate in substance -- that branch changed zero production code by its own change_surface section, and it is merged (0bd718f is on main) -- but "already records ... for main" overstates by one step. Worth stating rather than glossing.
WHERE THE CLAIM DOES NOT REACH, stated plainly: the report has 16 failures; this run has 15; they are NOT the same set. 13 of 15 are covered (10 IdentityMigrationTest + 3 Check.TestTest). The 2 too_many_connections failures (SandboxPoolTest, Definitions.MigrationsTest) appear NOWHERE in that report -- the report's own environment section records `grep -c too_many_connections` = 0 for its run. Conversely the report's 3 UNATTRIBUTED failures (EngineConcurrencyTest, Definitions.RollbackTest, IdentityTest) do not appear in this run's 15. So report-matching alone does NOT dispose of the red gate, and a verdict resting on it would be attributing 2 failures on judgement -- which is what core-directives forbids.

THE DECISIVE ANSWER DOES NOT NEED REPORT-MATCHING, AND I ESTABLISHED IT HERE. Two commands, run by me:
  (i) git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- '*.ex' '*.exs' lib/ priv/ config/ mix.exs mix.lock test/
      -> exactly one path: lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md (markdown). Zero compiled source, zero test source, zero config, zero migration, mix.lock unchanged.
  (ii) grep -rn over lib/ and test/ (--include=*.ex --include=*.exs) for requirement_status|anti-patterns|core-directives|AGENT_SYSTEM|doc-updater|release-validator|TASK_QUEUE|WF-02_requirement
      -> exactly ONE hit: a @moduledoc string at test/letflow/migration_filenames_test.exs:4. Prose in a docstring, not a File.read. ELIXIR-DEV's claim (b) is confirmed independently.
Therefore the compiled application and the test corpus on this branch are BYTE-IDENTICAL to main, and no causal path exists from this diff to any test outcome. VERDICT: this branch adds no failure that main does not already have. That is established by causal impossibility, which is strictly stronger than baseline matching and, unlike it, covers all 15 including the 2 connection-saturation failures. Those 2 are environmental (max_connections=100, container up 11h, psql itself refused after the run) and would occur identically on main under the same conditions.
WHAT I DO NOT ESTABLISH, so Step Final is not built on more than this supports: I did NOT run main, and I make no claim about main's exact failure count today. main is red (ISS-0109 instrumented, ISS-0116 open). Step Final may proceed on "adds no new failure", NOT on "the gate is green" -- those are different findings and only the first is in evidence.
THIS ARGUMENT EXPIRES AT STEP 4 -- flagging because it is easy to miss: the moment TEST-DESIGNER adds test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs and test/support/status_history.ex, the branch is no longer "zero .exs" and the causal-impossibility proof no longer holds. TEST-RUNNER MUST re-establish the baseline at Step 4c on its own evidence; it may not inherit this finding. Recommend it also run the invariant file in isolation (no DB needed) so A0-A8 are observed independently of ISS-0109's noise.
FOR ORCH / ISSUE_QUEUE, not for this run to fix: the 2 too_many_connections failures and the report's 3 unattributed ones (EngineConcurrencyTest, RollbackTest, IdentityTest) should be triaged under ISS-0116 rather than absorbed into "the known environmental set" by habit. The report was careful not to wave them through; that care should not be lost downstream.

=== E. THE TWO INFO ITEMS -- BOTH DISPOSITIONED ===
INFO-1 (AGENT_SYSTEM.md:105) -> UPHELD AS A MINOR. ELIXIR-DEV was right to use section 10.6's exact text and right to flag it rather than improve it silently; that is the correct instruction-following call and I would have flagged a silent improvement. But the resulting sentence IS misleading, and more so than "not false": it reads "`docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` remains the append-only event history (...), kept in bounded volumes behind `docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml`." Volume 1 is now CLOSED and is emphatically NOT bounded -- 361,376 bytes, the very file whose unboundedness is this issue. Section 10.6 fixed the parenthetical and left the subject stale. An agent landing on this line alone is told the closed volume is the append target, which is the precise error this run exists to prevent. NOT a gate blocker (it is the design's own approved text, faithfully applied, and the index/header/doc-updater sites all point correctly), but it should be corrected before merge. Suggested replacement, one line, no other change:
  "The requirement run history remains append-only (`started`/`done`/`blocked`/`cancelled`/`revised`/`verified`), kept in bounded volumes behind `docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml`; `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` is volume 1, closed."
Routing: ORCH's call -- either fold into Step 4's commit or take it directly under ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10's sizing rule. I did not edit it (I edit no file but this handoff).
INFO-2 (TASK_QUEUE.md re-wrap) -> ACCEPTED, NO ACTION. Verified in the diff: the replacement text matches section 10.4 word for word, and the only other change is that the trailing "A prod deployment (`queue.ai-dala.com`) is not yet planned -- test only, per T-0107's notes." sentence moved to a new line. Not one word altered, nothing added, nothing dropped. Re-wrapping prose to keep line length after splicing exact replacement text is normal editing, not a divergence, and ELIXIR-DEV was right that it needed disclosing rather than assuming.

=== F. TYPE-SAFETY (my mandate item 3) ===
Nothing to file. No transition logic, no state, no struct in this diff. The change moves an invariant from prose toward mechanical enforcement, which is the same direction item 3 points; the concrete instrument is TEST-DESIGNER's at Step 4. No docs/issues/ entry warranted.

=== G. FILES MODIFIED BY THIS STEP ===
Exactly one: handoffs/WF03-ISS0119-20260821/step-03d-reviewer.json. handoffs/orchestrator.log carries uncommitted ORCH edits and was left untouched, as instructed. My commit names its path explicitly.
